verdict: SAMPLE COMPLEXITY DIVERGES AT THE WALL (② EXP-12): the frontier's SAMPLING axis is now a QUANTITY, not a binary abstain. Resolving the contextual verdict for a Werner state a margin delta = CHSH-2 above the wall needs N_resolve samples, and N_resolve DIVERGES as delta -> 0: from 400 samples at delta=0.6 down to 409600 samples at delta=0.02, a 1024x growth. The log-log slope is -1.96 ~ -2, matching the derivable law N_resolve ~ 1/delta^2 (empirical CHSH noise ~ 1/sqrt(N), so you need delta > ~1.96*SE). This is a critical-slowing-down analog: near a decision boundary the data cost to decide blows up as an inverse-square power law. With this, all THREE frontier axes are instrumented -- discoverability (145), predictability (152), and sampling (153) -- the last as a measured sample-complexity divergence.
